cleanIntro: A striker-fired 9mm that field strips without a takedown button: rotate the lever, ease the slide off the frame, and the recoil spring and barrel lift out of it. FN's book is written for the whole 509 series, so two of its steps are conditional on what your particular pistol carries — a manual safety, a threaded barrel — and the walk asks you to settle both before you touch the lever.

steps.title: Read the slide: this book is for a pistol with 509 in its name
steps.action: Look at the model designation rolled on the slide before you start. If the pistol does not carry 509 in its naming convention, or does not look like the pistol drawn in this manual, stop and get FN's book for the pistol you actually have.
steps.prose: FN publishes separate manuals for the 502, the 503, the 510 and 545, the High Power and the Reflex, and their takedown levers rotate different amounts in different directions — the 502 wants 108 degrees, the High Power 90 degrees counterclockwise. A 509 procedure applied to a sibling is not a near miss, it is the wrong lever travel on a different lockwork. The specification table in the back of this book lists the 509, the 509 Tactical, the 509 Midsize, the 509 Midsize MRD and the 509 Compact MRD, so a plain full-size 509 is squarely inside it.
steps.quote: IF YOUR FN PISTOL DOES NOT HAVE 509 IN ITS NAMING CONVENTION OR IF THE APPEARANCE OF THE PISTOL DOES NOT CORRESPOND TO THE ILLUSTRATIONS IN THIS OWNER’S MANUAL CONTACT YOUR DEALER, DEPARTMENT ARMORER OR CONTACT FN DIRECTLY TO OBTAIN THE OWNER’S MANUAL THAT HAS BEEN WRITTEN SPECIFICALLY FOR YOUR PISTOL.
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — Foreword block, p.2

steps.title: Magazine out first, and pull it if it hangs
steps.action: Point the muzzle somewhere safe, keep your finger off the trigger, press the ambidextrous magazine release and take the magazine out of the pistol. If it does not drop free, pull down on the base plate while you hold the release in.
steps.prose: The 509's magazine release sits behind the trigger inside a raised guard, so it takes a deliberate press rather than a brush — that guard is there to stop the release being tripped if the pistol is dropped or pressed against a flat surface. A 17-round magazine full of 9mm is heavy enough to stick in a dry, dirty magazine well, and a magazine that is only half out is still feeding the pistol. Get it clear of the frame and set it down away from the bench before the slide moves.
steps.quote: Press the magazine release and remove the magazine. If the magazine does not drop out of the pistol, pull on the magazine base plate while pressing the magazine release (Figure 12).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §6.3 Unloading, step 1, p.22
steps.warn: FN's order is magazine first, then chamber. Working the slide with the magazine still seated chambers a fresh round instead of clearing one.

steps.title: Rack the chamber empty and lock the slide back
steps.action: Pull the slide fully to the rear so any chambered round is ejected, then press the slide stop up and let the slide settle back against it so it stays open.
steps.prose: Do this in one firm stroke — a short pull can drag a round part way out and let it drop back into the chamber. Both slide stop levers work; the 509's stop is fully ambidextrous, so the thumb of your shooting hand can hold it up while the support hand eases the slide back onto it. With the slide locked open the pistol is in the condition every later step in the book assumes.
steps.quote: Lock the slide to the rear by pressing the slide stop up and allowing the slide to rest against the slide stop retaining it to the rear (Figure 13).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §6.3 Unloading, step 2, p.22

steps.title: Look into the chamber and the magazine well, and do not trust the red dot
steps.action: With the slide locked open, look into the ejection port at the chamber and down into the magazine well. Confirm with your eyes that both are empty; if the light is poor, put a finger in.
steps.prose: The 509's loaded chamber indicator is the extractor itself — a chambered case pushes it out and exposes a red dot on the right side of the slide behind the ejection port. It is a useful tell that the chamber is loaded and a bad way to decide it is empty, because the dot can be obscured or worn. This is the last check before the trigger gets pressed later in the strip, so make it a look, not an assumption.
steps.quote: Inspect the chamber and magazine well to ensure no cartridge is present. Remember, merely removing the magazine does not mean the chamber is unloaded (Figure 14).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §6.3 Unloading, step 3, p.22
steps.warn: FN's own words on the indicator: THE RED DOT THAT INDICATES A LOADED CHAMBER CAN BECOME OBSCURED. DO NOT DEPEND ON THE RED INDICATOR TO DETERMINE THE UNLOADED CONDITION OF THE PISTOL.

steps.title: Settle whether your 509 has a manual safety
steps.action: Look at the rear of the frame just above the grip. If there is a small lever on each side there, your pistol has the optional manual safety; put it down into the fire position, exposing the red dot, so it is out of the way for disassembly. If there is no lever, this pistol has none and nothing here applies.
steps.prose: FN builds the 509 both ways and says so with an explicit qualifier on the section heading, so the manual will not tell you which one is in your hand. It matters at the bench because the safety blocks the sear carrier and trigger assembly, and the strip includes a deliberate trigger press — with the safety up the striker will not release and you will be pushing a slide that refuses to come forward. FN also warns the safety cannot be engaged with the trigger held to the rear, so do not try to put it back on mid-strip.
steps.aside: FN's note on the frame marking: the red dot showing means the pistol will fire, but the dot can become obscured or damaged, so it is not the thing you rely on to know the pistol's condition.
steps.quote: 9.2 MANUAL SAFETY (APPLICABLE ONLY TO PISTOLS WITH A MANUAL SAFETY)
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §9.2 heading, p.30

steps.title: Threaded barrel? The thread protector comes off before the lever
steps.action: Look at the muzzle. If this 509 has a threaded barrel, unscrew the thread protector or muzzle device counterclockwise and set it aside now, before anything else moves.
steps.prose: FN qualifies its threaded-barrel section the same way it qualifies the safety, because only some 509s are cut for it — the threads are ½"-28 and the protector is meant to be on the gun whenever a can or a device is not. Take it off first: a protector left on adds length in front of the slide and gets in the way when the slide runs forward off the frame, and its threads are exactly where fouling collects on a suppressed pistol. If your muzzle is plain, skip this and go to the lever.
steps.aside: FN's own qualifier on the section: 9.8 THREADED BARREL (APPLICABLE ONLY TO PISTOLS WITH THREADED BARRELS).
steps.quote: Remove the thread protector or muzzle device if the pistol is equipped with a threaded barrel (Figure 40).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, step 3, p.36

steps.title: Rotate the takedown lever a full quarter turn and a bit more
steps.action: With the slide still locked open, rotate the takedown lever roughly 100 degrees clockwise. It should turn under thumb pressure and stop with a definite feel; do not force it past that.
steps.prose: The 509 lever wants more than a right angle — 100 degrees, not 90 — and stopping short is the commonest reason the slide then refuses to come off the frame. Keep the slide locked back while you turn it; the lever cannot rotate against a closed slide. If it will not move, the slide has crept forward off the slide stop, so reset that first rather than leaning on the lever.
steps.quote: Rotate the takedown lever approximately 100 deg. clockwise (Figure 41).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, step 4, p.36

steps.title: Release the striker with the slide and frame in line
steps.action: Take the slide in one hand, release it off the slide stop and ease it forward — do not let it run. Keep the rear of the slide level with the rear of the frame, point the muzzle in a safe direction, and press the trigger to release the striker. The slide moves forward slightly as it goes.
steps.prose: This is the step that makes people uneasy and it is the one FN prints a warning against: the pistol must be completely unloaded before the trigger is pressed, which is why the chamber was checked by eye two steps ago. Keeping the slide and frame rear faces aligned is what lets the striker drop cleanly; let the slide run too far forward and the sear catches it again. If the striker recocks by accident, ease the slide back into line and press the trigger again rather than trying to pull the slide off a cocked striker.
steps.quote: While keeping the rear of the slide and rear of the frame in alignment, point the muzzle in a safe direction and press the trigger to release the striker. The slide will move forward slightly when released (Figure 43).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, step 5, p.37
steps.warn: THE PISTOL MUST BE COMPLETELY UNLOADED TO PERFORM STEP 5. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THIS WARNING COULD RESULT IN SERIOUS INJURY OR DEATH.

steps.title: Slide forward and off the frame
steps.action: With the striker down, run the slide forward and lift it away from the frame rails. It comes off as one assembly with the barrel and recoil spring still inside it.
steps.prose: There should be no resistance at all now — if the slide binds at the front of the rails, the striker has recocked or the takedown lever has crept back, and forcing it only rounds the rail edges. Support the slide as it comes free rather than letting it drop; the recoil spring assembly inside is still compressed against the barrel lug. Put the frame down with the magazine well up so nothing rolls off the bench.
steps.quote: After releasing the striker, you can remove the slide by pulling the slide forward and away from the frame.
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, step 6, p.37

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly out, small end first
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down. Take hold of the small spring at the front of the recoil spring assembly, lift that end up out of its seat, and draw the whole assembly out of the slide.
steps.prose: The 509's captive recoil spring assembly sits in a recess in the front of the slide with its rear end centred on the barrel lug — grasp the small forward spring, not the middle, or you will be pulling against the compression rather than releasing it. It comes out with a short lift and a pull, no tools. Keep it as one unit: it is not meant to come apart, and a guide rod separated from its springs is a service item.
steps.quote: Hold the slide upside down, grasp the small spring of the recoil spring assembly then lift the recoil spring assembly up and out of the slide (Figure 45).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, step 7, p.38

steps.title: Barrel up, around the extractor, then back and out
steps.action: Grip the barrel by its lug underneath, lift it up and swing it around the extractor, then slide it rearward out of the slide.
steps.prose: It is a three-part motion and skipping the middle one is what makes a 509 barrel feel jammed — lift first so the lug clears its seat, move it around the extractor claw rather than into it, and only then take it back out of the breech end. Forcing the barrel straight back with the lug still down loads the extractor sideways, which is the one part in the slide you do not want to spring. That is the strip finished.
steps.quote: Grasp the barrel by its lug, lift it up and around the extractor and slide the barrel rearward out of the slide (Figure 46).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, step 9, p.38

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Four groups on the bench: frame, slide, barrel, recoil spring assembly — plus the thread protector if this one wears a threaded barrel. FN says that is enough for a thorough clean and that anything further is an armorer's job.
steps.prose: From here you can reach every surface the cleaning section names: the bore from the chamber end, the breech face and extractor, the slide rails on both sides, the barrel's unlock surface and its outside, and the frame's magazine well. FN's cleaning interval for hard use is every 500 rounds, and a suppressed or dirty-ammunition 509 earns it sooner. The deeper procedures the book publishes — magazine, backstrap, optics plate, muzzle device, magazine release — sit behind Deep Clean.
steps.quote: This level of disassembly is sufficient to perform a thorough cleaning. Disassembly beyond the instructions provided in this manual should only be carried out by a qualified armorer.
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, closing note, p.38

deepSteps.title: Magazine down to its parts, floor plate catch first
deepSteps.action: Confirm the magazine is empty. Point its base away from you, press the floor plate catch in through the hole in the floor plate, and slide the plate forward off the body while your hand caps the spring. Then lift out the catch, the spring and the follower.
deepSteps.prose: The 509 magazine spring is long and stiff — a 17-round column of 9mm needs it to be — and it will launch the floor plate catch across the room if the plate is allowed to jump. Trap it with your palm as the plate slides forward and release the pressure gradually. Match the follower's angle to the feed lips when it goes back, and check the catch's tab is standing proud in the floor plate before the magazine goes back in the pistol.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the floor plate catch, magazine spring and follower from the magazine body (Figure 60).
deepSteps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.4 Magazine disassembly, step 2, p.43
deepSteps.warn: CAUTION: THE MAGAZINE SPRING IS UNDER TENSION. WEAR EYE PROTECTION AND KEEP THE BOTTOM OF THE MAGAZINE POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION.

deepSteps.title: Know which magazines this book actually covers
deepSteps.action: Before stripping any magazine, check that it is one this manual describes. A 509 magazine not covered here should have arrived with an addendum, either in this manual or with the magazine itself; if you have neither, get the information from FN before taking it apart.
deepSteps.prose: The 509 family runs several magazine patterns — the standard is 17 rounds with witness holes down the back, and the parts list separately catalogues 24-round, 15-round and Midsize and Compact bodies. They do not all come apart the same way, and a floor plate catch from one pattern is not a licence to lever at another. This is FN's own carve-out and it is the reason the strip above is written for the magazine the book draws.
deepSteps.quote: FN 509 magazines not specifically covered in this manual should be covered by an addendum included with this manual or with the magazine.
deepSteps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §9.6 Magazine, p.33

deepSteps.title: Backstrap off, roll pin punch only
deepSteps.action: With the frame empty, drive the backstrap retaining pin out with a small 5/64" roll pin punch, then slide the backstrap off the dovetail at the rear of the frame.
deepSteps.prose: The pin is a roll pin and a solid punch or a nail will collapse it — use the 5/64" roll pin punch FN names or leave it alone. Coming off gives you the grip channel underneath, which is where sweat and lint collect on a carried pistol and where the polymer is never reached by a bore brush. On the way back, seat the backstrap so the gap at the top closes and line its pin hole up with the slot in the dovetail before the pin goes anywhere near it.
deepSteps.quote: Using a small 5/64" roll pin punch, push out the backstrap
deepSteps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.3 Backstrap removal, step 1, p.41

deepSteps.title: Optic or slide cap: screws dry, no threadlocker
deepSteps.action: If you are taking the optic or slide cap off to clean under it, back the two screws out counterclockwise, lift off the optic, the MRD plate and the o-ring, and clean the mounting surface on top of the slide. Put it back with all lubricant removed from the screws and the screw holes, o-ring in its recess, and tighten with the supplied T10 Torx to finger pressure.
deepSteps.prose: FN's low-profile mounting system is self-locking, so threadlocker is not just unnecessary here — it can seize the screws hard enough that the optic or cap cannot be removed later without damage. Oil in the screw holes is the opposite failure and just as real: a lubricated thread lets the screws walk under recoil. Clean and dry is the whole specification, and the o-ring has to be sandwiched between slide and plate or the joint will not seal.
deepSteps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.5 Optics mounting system, note, p.47

deepSteps.title: Threaded muzzle: caliber, thread pattern, and the Nielsen device
deepSteps.action: If this 509 wears a can or a muzzle device, take it off for cleaning and check on the way back that it is rated for the caliber marked on the back of the barrel, that it has ½"-28 right-hand threads, and that its bore lines up with the barrel's with nothing in the bullet's path.
deepSteps.prose: A device with a bore smaller than the cartridge, or one threaded on crooked, is the failure that wrecks the can and the pistol together — FN spells that out at length in this section. Worth knowing at the bench too: a suppressor without a Nielsen device will fire safely but will not cycle the slide, so a 509 that suddenly short-strokes after a clean is usually telling you about the mount, not the gun. Suppressed shooting also fouls faster, which is FN's stated reason for cleaning more often.
deepSteps.quote: If a suppressor is attached to the barrel without a Nielsen device, the pistol can be safely fired but will not cycle properly.
deepSteps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.6 Suppressor and muzzle device installation and use, p.50

cleaning.name: BARREL & BORE
tasks: Brush or spray solvent into the bore and chamber and let it sit a few minutes before any patch goes through
Rod, jag and patches from the chamber end only — FN is explicit that cleaning from the muzzle risks the crown and the accuracy with it
Patch until they come out clean, then a patch moistened with preservative oil through the bore to protect it until next use
Lightly oil the outside of the barrel and the unlock surface; that is a bearing face, not decoration

cleaning.name: SLIDE, BREECH FACE & FRAME
tasks: Brush and solvent on the breech face, under the extractor and around the ejection port, where primer and powder residue collects

Wipe the slide rails on both sides, then a drop of lightweight gun oil on each — the 509 lubrication diagram calls for both rails, the striker block, the sear, the disconnect cam, the cartridge guide and the unlock block
Soft cloth into the magazine well to take out lint and debris; keep solvent off the polymer frame
Check the disassembled parts for wear or damage as you go, and ask FN about anything you are unsure of rather than reassembling it

cleaning.name: AFTER, AND BEFORE THE NEXT RANGE TRIP
tasks: Never soak the pistol in solvent or lubricant, and go light with oil — FN warns that too much interferes with function
Wipe the outside down to remove dirt, fingerprints and excess lubricant before it goes away
Clean and lubricate after every use, or every 500 rounds in intensive shooting; sooner if it has seen salt, sand, moisture, dirty ammunition or a suppressor
Run a dry patch through the bore before shooting to take out the storage oil

reassembly: Barrel into the slide first: muzzle through the barrel hole from the inside, let it drop down, then slide it back to the breech face until the lug drops into its locked position.
Refit the thread protector or muzzle device if this 509 has a threaded barrel, turning it clockwise onto the ½"-28 threads.
Large end of the recoil spring assembly against the recess in the front of the slide, compress it, and seat the back of the guide centred on the front of the barrel lug.
Guide the slide and barrel onto the frame rails, run it fully to the rear and lock it there on the slide stop.
Rotate the takedown lever back upward to lock frame and slide together, then release the slide and let it run forward.
Test slide stop, trigger, magazine release and — if fitted — the manual safety before the pistol is loaded.
fncheck: With the pistol empty and reassembled: the takedown lever should sit flush and refuse to rotate against a closed slide; the slide should run fully forward into battery under its own spring and lock back on either slide stop lever; the trigger should reset with a click when the slide is cycled; the magazine release should drop an empty magazine free from the well; and on a pistol so equipped the manual safety levers should snap into each position on their detent — remembering FN's note that the safety cannot be engaged with the trigger held to the rear.
